rv.q: I am happy report that this is a very funny 'Nunsense,' as directed by the veteran performer E. Faye Butler...
I suspect that today's audiences will find this spiritually uplifting, Ecclesiastically-based musical comedy as much fun as audiences did over 40 years ago.
You really cannot go wrong with 'Nunsense.' 'Nunsense' delivers all of this and more and will be sure to keep you smiling from start to finish.
"Nunsense" is light entertainment that is sure to tickle one's funny bone, supported by a cast that delivers a heavenly performance.
Nunsense is a fun idea, but the script fails to execute it satisfyingly.

While "Nunsense" is billed as Musical Comedy, with a book, music and lyrics by Dan Coggin, I think of it as more of a revue with a story, albeit a very weak one, but the show is great fun, even if you are Jewish. Luckily, my co-host and good buddy is a devout Catholic, so I am able to get any notes that may have been side jokes over my head.
Ultimately, this production succeeds despite Nunsense rather than because of it.
